overview: This 467-page file documents U.S. handling of Japanese training ships and naval transports visiting American ports in 1936–1937. Diplomatic notes and interdepartmental correspondence trace itineraries, port courtesies, customs and immigration arrangements, and visits altered by naval maneuvers, repairs, and illness. It also records a dispute over Japanese sailors in Seattle’s Fourth of July parade, Customs complaints involving the Erimo, and confidential exchanges with the Netherlands about Japanese naval oil purchases.
interest: The file shows how routine port visits exposed diplomatic sensitivities, enforcement disputes, and concern over Japan’s naval oil supply.
